thread:
maya: Heads up — noticed a regression after the policy-template v2 rollout. Nested group inheritance isn't applying for some service accounts. Observed in staging and a couple of Dedicated customers.
samir: Uh, can you repro? steps + logs?
maya: Yes repro steps below. Happens when a service account is a member of Group A which is nested into Group B and Group B has a role binding. The effective role is missing.
maya: Repro steps:
1) create group A and group B
2) add service-account:sa-ml to group A
3) nest group A under group B
4) bind role `inference.viewer` to group B
5) call `GET /v1/principals/sa-ml/effective_roles`
maya: observed output: `[]` but expected `inference.viewer`.
maya: Logs from auth-service (truncated):
```
2026-03-19T15:41:02Z auth DEBUG resolve_groups: input=[sa-ml]
2026-03-19T15:41:02Z auth DEBUG expand_group: group=A -> parent=B
2026-03-19T15:41:02Z auth WARN compute_effective_roles: group-membership-empty-cache
2026-03-19T15:41:02Z auth ERROR role_lookup: role-binding not found for group B (binding exists in DB id=8421)
```
samir: That ERROR jumps out. Could be a cache invalidation bug in the new policy template codepath. Any recent changes to group cache keys?
maya: Yes — policy-template v2 added a fingerprint field to role-binding protobuf which changed cache key derivation. The cache expirer expects legacy key shape, so mismatches.
alex: Sounds plausible. Short-term mitigation: disable policy-template-v2 flag for affected clusters (staging + affected Dedicated tenants) and flush auth cache. Longer term: patch cache key to include fingerprint.
maya: Confirmed disabling the flag in staging fixed the repro. I'll prepare a rollback PR and a hotfix for the cache key algorithm.
samir: For customers already affected, we should provide a mitigation doc and an API workaround: explicitly bind role to the service account (not just via nested groups). Example CLI:
```
redwood iam bind --principal sa:sa-ml --role inference.viewer --scope project:demo
```
alex: SDK note: rbac client 2.1.2 still uses legacy cache key. I have a branch with 2.1.3 that preserves fingerprint in the cache key and has unit tests for nested groups. Recommend posting an SDK patch and tagging release-2.1.3.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0319-01 — "RBAC nested-group regression after policy-template v2". Pager duty notified.
sec-eng-bot: Added audit labels: [rbac:regression, priority:high, affected:dedicated]. Added link to internal postmortem draft: https://internal/docs/incidents/INC-2026-0319-01
maya: Action items:
- maya: open rollback PR for policy-template v2 flag (in flight)
- alex: open SDK 2.1.3 PR + release notes
- samir: update auth-service cache key logic + unit tests
- maya: draft customer mitigation note and add CLI workaround to docs/rbac/role-mapping.md
samir: Also add an audit log enrichment to include resolved group ancestry in debug mode — will help triage similar issues.
alex: I'll add a small migration test to infra that creates a nested group topology and runs effective_roles check on each change — catch regressions in CI.
maya: Thanks all. I'll ping once rollback is merged. :thumbsup:
samir: thx — please @channel the customer note when ready.
maya: Will do.
